key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for tandem photovoltaics, delivering 24.0% efficiency in four-terminal devices.
engineering_relevance: Improved charge extraction in thicker AgBiS2 nanocrystal films supports their development as stable, scalable near-infrared sub-cells.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated, thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports modeled triple-junction efficiencies above 47.5%, measured four-terminal efficiency of 24.0%, monolithic voltage addition, and retention of >90% initial efficiency after three months in dry air without encapsulation.
watch_item: The >47.5% efficiency is a modeled projection, and dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under operating conditions.
paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
